data.title: Swiss lobby seeks changes to government's proposed banking overhaul
data.description:
The Swiss Bankers Association on Thursday said Switzerland's proposed banking stability reforms were too far-reaching and unbalanced, arguing they went beyond the failings exposed by the 2023 Credit Suisse collapse, and urged changes to be made.

  • The SBA said it backed steps to improve access to central bank liquidity in a crisis, but rejected broader sanction powers for Swiss financial market regulator FINMA

  • The government proposals were made following the demise of Credit Suisse and its subsequent takeover by UBS

  • The SBA also rejected the introduction of a senior managers regime as proposed by the government

  • Around 30 measures in the package could raise costs for banks, customers and the wider economy, SBA said

  • FINMA would get disproportionately far-reaching new powers under the proposal, it added

data.title: GomSpace continues to support advanced lunar exploration with an 8 MEUR (89.1 MSEK) contract with a leading North American space company
data.description:
The second phase accelerates development of dual-satellite lunar mission for resource prospecting.

STOCKHOLM, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- GomSpace has secured an 8 MEUR contract for the second phase of a lunar mission program for a Leading North American Space Company, reinforcing its role in advanced deep space exploration initiatives. The contract for the first phase was announced on January 9, 2026.

This lunar mission will deploy two satellites into orbit around the Moon to conduct resource prospecting in support of future lunar exploration. This second phase advances the mission towards full operational capability in lunar orbit, ultimately leading to end-of-mission operations around the Moon. The delivery is scheduled for late 2027.

Building on its established heritage, GomSpace will leverage its experience from ESA's Hera mission, including the Juventas CubeSat, to support the development of high-reliability systems required for complex deep space missions. The program further strengthens GomSpace's ambitions in advanced exploration missions beyond Earth orbit.

Key upcoming milestones include the Critical Design Review, satellite payload integration in the United States, and launch activities to be conducted in the United States.

"This contract marks an important milestone for GomSpace and highlights our capability to deliver reliable, high-performance systems for complex exploration missions. By leveraging our deep-space heritage, we are proud to contribute to advancing lunar exploration and enabling future resource utilization beyond Earth," says Edgar Milic, VP Advanced Mission at GomSpace.

This contract supports GomSpace's strategic progression towards delivering complete mission solutions, reinforcing its position as a key partner in international space exploration programs.

GomSpace also has key operations in Luxembourg, France, and the United States. GomSpace develops and delivers advanced systems and services that enable governments, commercial enterprises, and research institutions to achieve their objectives in space. The company's expertise covers satellite subsystems, complete small satellite missions, and satellite operations, providing solutions that support smarter, faster, and more affordable access to space.

data.title: PepsiCo Romania taps Rezolv for power from 431-MW Vifor wind farm
data.description:
November 19 (Renewables Now) - Actis and Mubadala-backed renewables developer Rezolv Energy has attracted PepsiCo Romania as a power off-taker of the 192-MW first phase of its 461-MW Vifor wind farm project in Romania.

The beverage and food company will procure 13 GWh of electricity annually under a 10-year virtual power purchase agreement (VPPA), Rezolv said on Thursday. According to its estimates, the contracted power volumes are equal to the annual consumption of around 8,000 Romanian households.

The long-term VPPA will diversify PepsiCo Romania’s energy sourcing and support its business resilience in the evolving energy landscape. It comes two years after the company invested USD 2.1 million (EUR 1.9m) to install more than 3,000 photovoltaic (PV) panels at its facilities in Dragomiresti, Popesti-Leordeni and Covasna.

Commenting on the arrangement, Alastair Hammond, Rezolv Energy’s CEO said: “Corporate demand for clean power is growing rapidly, and virtual PPAs like this are helping to accelerate the country’s energy transition.”

The Vifor wind farm is being built in southeastern Romania’s Buzau County and will be one of Europe’s largest ones, once all of its 72 turbines are fully commissioned. The plant’s initial phase, comprising 30 Vestas turbines, was energised last month, while Phase 2 is planned to enter commercial operations in the summer of 2027. T-Mobile Czech Republic, Slovak Telekom, CE Colo Czech Republic, Belgium's Bekaert, Italian utility A2A and Etem Gestamp have already lined up to buy power from the complex.

(USD 1.0 = EUR 0.910)

data.title: Deutsche Bank CEO says clients calm after data leak
data.description:
Deutsche Bank CEO Christian Sewing on Thursday said clients were calm after a major leak of internal records and that Germany's largest lender was not seeing an impact on business.

The leak ​of 15 million internal records reported this week has renewed scrutiny of the German lender's past dealings ‌with clients ⁠including Russian oligarchs, US President Donald Trump and sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

"If you ask, what is the client reaction since Tuesday? Very calm," Sewing said at a financial conference.

"We have built trust and confidence with our clients," he added, noting that the bank was not currently seeing any impact on business.

The ordeal dealt a major setback to ​Sewing's efforts to restore the lender's reputation.

"This is a totally different bank ... Certain issues happened in the past. They have been worked on," he said.

data.title: East Timor eyes boost in business funding through instant payment system
data.description:
By Jun Yuan Yong

East Timor, one of the world's poorest countries, hopes to close a funding gap for its small businesses and help integration with the regional bloc ASEAN through a new instant payment system, its central bank governor said on Thursday.

  • East Timor needs to spur private sector economic activity, as a big proportion of its economy is driven by informal businesses unable to secure loans, Governor Hélder Lopes told Reuters

  • Through digital payments, a system for which was introduced in September, lenders can use transaction information to assess if businesses are viable for financing, Lopes added

  • Asia's youngest country formally joined the Association of Southeast Asian Nations last year after a 14-year wait to become the bloc's 11th member

  • East Timor's 2025 gross domestic product was about $1.9 billion, according to the World Bank, a fraction of ASEAN's combined GDP of more than $3.8 trillion

  • Lopes said the country was seeking to "level up" to ASEAN's standard to support financial and economic integration and digitalisation

  • "Our financial sector is highly liquid and we have a huge amount of excess liquidity but the issue is channelling this to our economic activities," he said on the sidelines of a fintech event in Singapore

  • The World Bank in a report last year said East Timor was entering a "potentially transformative" economic chapter but needs to move beyond oil and gas and improve private sector productivity

  • Lopes also said East Timor, which uses the US dollar, has benefited from the strength of the dollar against the rupiah of neighbouring Indonesia, the source of most of its imports

data.title: Copper Remains Under Pressure After Wave of Selling — Market Talk
data.description: Copper prices remain near their lowest level since April following a broad selloff across commodity markets, driven by a stronger U.S. dollar and growing concerns over AI-related investment. In early European trading, three-month copper futures on the LME fall 0.7% to $12,531.50 a metric ton, putting the metal on track for a weekly decline of 9%. "Concerns around the pace of data centre build out are weighing significantly on copper, even if not much has changed for 2027 build plans," analysts at Morgan Stanley say. The weakness comes despite constrained global mine supply and tight inventories in China. Meanwhile, expectations of higher interest rates are adding to the pressure, as elevated borrowing costs could weigh on industrial investment and strengthen the dollar, making dollar-denominated commodities more expensive for overseas buyers. (giulia.petroni@wsj.com)
